The user wants a five-sentence explanation of why the sky is blue. Let me craft a clear, accurate explanation in exactly five sentences.

1. Sunlight contains all colors of visible light, which together appear white.
2. When sunlight enters Earth's atmosphere, it interacts with nitrogen and oxygen molecules.
3. These molecules scatter shorter wavelengths (blue and violet) much more strongly than longer wavelengths (red and orange) — this is called Rayleigh scattering, where the amount of scattering is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the wavelength.
4. Although violet light is scattered even more than blue, our eyes are less sensitive to violet, and some of it is absorbed by the ozone layer, so the scattered light we perceive is predominantly blue.
5. This scattered blue light is what reaches our eyes from all directions in the sky, giving it its characteristic blue appearance.
